candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is pustular psoriasis. AGEP due to hydroxychloroquine is a competing diagnosis that shares clinical and histological features (subcorneal neutrophilic pustules, drug trigger) but is a different diagnostic entity. However, the clinical scenario—prior episode resolving over three months (longer than typical AGEP resolution of <15 days), no psoriasis history yet drug-provoked generalized pustular eruption with systemic features—raises the possibility of drug-induced pustular psoriasis. The reference explicitly names pustular psoriasis, not AGEP. C001 asserts AGEP, which is an incompatible subtype/scope relative to the benchmark of pustular psoriasis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: AGEP is a distinct drug-induced pustular eruption; pustular psoriasis is a separate entity, though both share subcorneal pustulation histologically

case_quality_flags: Clinically ambiguous: AGEP vs drug-induced pustular psoriasis overlap; prolonged resolution course (~3 months) favors pustular psoriasis over AGEP; no personal/family psoriasis history noted but does not exclude pustular psoriasis
